description: we're team zim from chittagong, bangladesh.
summary: Chader Buri is an interactive lunar landing-site navigator for the Moon's south pole. It helps students, educators and early mission planners see how a landing site, an arrival date and the equipment together decide whether a mission gets enough sunlight, power and contact with Earth. Using NASA LRO LOLA terrain and JPL Horizons Sun and Earth positions, a deterministic engine compares 14 south-pole sites hour by hour, draws the Sun's and Earth's paths over each site's real skyline, models battery energy and Earth visibility, and searches every arrival hour for windows that meet the mission's requirements. Visitors can then walk the selected site in 3D. An AI guide, Chader Buri, inspired by the Bengali folk tale of the grandmother on the Moon, explains results in plain language, and every number she states must trace back to the calculation. Example: at Malapert Massif, the same lander arriving one week later drops from 28.1% to 5.2% minimum battery, below its 20% reserve.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Chader Buri answers the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge: compare landing sites and dates, and see the Sun and Earth against the local horizon for solar power and direct-to-Earth communication.

HOW IT WORKS

- Terrain: NASA LRO LOLA polar elevation models give each of 14 south-pole sites a 360-degree horizon profile traced out to 160 km, so a distant ridge that hides the Sun or Earth is part of the result.

- Sky: JPL Horizons (DE441) Sun and Earth positions for every site, every hour, September 2026 to December 2028. NAIF SPICE orientations drive the 3D scene.

- Mission model: the visitor sets duration, electrical load, panel area, battery and reserve, and sunlight and Earth-link limits. The engine reports whether the mission meets or misses each requirement and which constraint is tightest.

- Visual answer: the Sun's and Earth's paths over the whole mission are drawn on each site's measured skyline, solid where visible and dashed where hidden; a separate line shows how long the Sun and Earth are visible together (geometry only, not power or a radio link).

- Arrival search: checks every hourly arrival for up to 90 days and states exactly which range was searched.

- Communications: Earth visibility with Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra geometry and an X-band screening budget from the DSN 810-005 handbook.

- Surface: visitors walk the chosen site in 3D, move time to watch Earth set behind a ridge, aim an illustrative antenna and test solar-panel settings, with mission readouts on screen.

- AI guide: Chader Buri (Google Gemini 3.6 Flash) explains the calculated results in the visitor's language. A numeric-origin check rejects any reply containing a number that is not in the calculation, the screen or the conversation.

- Space weather: recent NASA DONKI reports, dated separately from the simulated mission.

EXAMPLE

Malapert Massif, 14 days, 1,200 W load, 3.08 m2 panels, 20% reserve: arriving 17 October 2026 keeps a 28.1% minimum battery; arriving 24 October drops it to 5.2%, although the Sun's centre is above the skyline in both windows. Visible sunlight alone does not guarantee enough energy.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students and educators see lunar conditions turned into decisions they can understand; early planners inspect trade-offs and assumptions in one place, with CSV exports and printable briefs.

SCIENTIFIC VALIDITY

Every result shows its basis beside the verdict: the nominal landing coordinate, hourly sampling, measured NASA terrain and JPL-predicted positions, and illustrative lander hardware. Regional illumination is benchmarked against published NASA results (Barker et al., 2021), and 46 automated test suites check the calculations. Results are screening predictions for planning and learning, not flight certification or a guaranteed radio link.

CREATIVITY

A guide character from Bengali folklore, a walkable surface tied to the mission, and a failure story (one week later, the same lander falls below reserve) that makes the physics memorable.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Vite, three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei, Tailwind CSS, Node.js API functions, Python data pipeline, Vercel hosting, Google Gemini API. 46 automated test suites check the calculations and interface.

Live: https://chader-buri.vercel.app
